title: Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 7.1 Call to Prophethood

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Prophethood began for Muhammad (S.A.W) in the Cave of Hira, when Angel Jibril (A.S.) brought the first verses of the Qur'an. In this sub-strand you will narrate that event, recite the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq, and see how those verses call Muslims to seek knowledge and to follow the Prophet's Sunnah.

## Strand 7.0: History of Islam
Sub-strand 7.1: Call to Prophethood
Suggested lessons: 4

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) describe the Prophet’s incidence at cave Hira with Angel Jibril (A.S.)
b) assess the significance of the first five verses revealed to Prophet (S.A.W) in relation to seeking knowledge
c) acknowledge the role of Prophet (S.A.W) as a messenger of Allah by emulating his Sunnah

## Key inquiry questions
1. What are the teachings of the first five verses revealed to Prophet (S.A.W)?

## Core competencies
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of writing and teamwork is enhanced as learners discuss the teachings from the first five verses of Suratul-Alaq, in pairs/groups, and write the points in their notebook.
• Learning to learn: the skill of sharing learnt knowledge is enhanced as learners read from reference material story on call to prophethood and narrates to others in class.
• Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with digital technology is enhanced as learners watch audio-visual clip/listen to a story from a digital device/resource person on Prophet’s experience at cave Hira.

## Values
• Respect: open mindedness enhanced as learners respect each other’s opinions while discussing the teachings from the first five verses of Suratul-Alaq.
• Responsibility: accountability enhanced as learners recite the first five verses of Suratul-Alaq, individually/in groups.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Empathy as learners learn how the Prophet (S.A.W) received divine guidance.

## Links to other learning areas
• The concept of reading first five verses of Surah-Alaq can be related to skills in English.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 7.0 History of Islam, Sub-strand 7.1 Call to Prophethood
• Sahih al-Bukhari: the Hadith of Aisha on the beginning of revelation in Cave Hira, Khadijah's comfort, and Waraqah ibn Nawfal
• Qur'an, Surah Al-Alaq 96:1-5

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: What happened in the Cave of Hira

LESSON 1: WHAT HAPPENED IN THE CAVE OF HIRA
===========================================

## What you will learn
• Describe how the Prophet (S.A.W) worshipped before the first revelation.
• Narrate the meeting with Angel Jibril (A.S.) in Cave Hira.

Curriculum outcomes: a) describe the Prophet’s incidence at cave Hira with Angel Jibril (A.S.)

## Introduction
Before anyone in Makkah called him a messenger, Muhammad (S.A.W) used to leave the city and sit alone in a cave to worship. What happened in that cave changed his life and the life of the world.

## Notes
### Before the call
Muhammad (S.A.W) was known in Makkah as Al-Amin, the Trustworthy. He was about forty years old. He disliked the idols of Makkah. He would take a little food and go to Cave Hira, on the mountain of light near Makkah, and stay there for nights, worshipping Allah and thinking. This worship before prophethood is called tahannuth in the Hadith.

### The angel's visit
The account is preserved in Sahih al-Bukhari from Aisha (R.A.). While the Prophet (S.A.W) was in the cave, Angel Jibril (A.S.) came to him and said, "Read."

The Prophet (S.A.W) replied, "I am not a reader."

The angel embraced him and pressed him hard until he could bear it no longer, then released him and said again, "Read." The Prophet (S.A.W) gave the same answer. This happened three times. After the third embrace, the angel recited the first verses of Surah Al-Alaq, beginning "Read in the name of your Lord who created."

### How he felt
The Prophet (S.A.W) came down from the cave with his heart trembling. He went to his wife Khadijah (R.A.) and said, "Cover me, cover me." She wrapped him until his fear eased. He told her what he had seen. He was not seeking fame. The weight of meeting an angel and receiving Allah's words was heavy, and he turned first to his home.

This event is the call to prophethood. From that hour he was the Messenger of Allah, sent to recite the Qur'an, teach the people, and call them to worship Allah alone.

## Key words
• Cave Hira — the cave near Makkah where the Prophet (S.A.W) first received revelation
• Jibril (A.S.) — the angel who brought the Qur'an from Allah to the Prophet (S.A.W)
• revelation — the message Allah sent down to His Prophet
• Al-Amin — the Trustworthy, the name the people of Makkah gave Muhammad (S.A.W)

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Put these events in order: (i) Jibril says Read (ii) the Prophet worships in Cave Hira (iii) the angel embraces him three times (iv) the first verses are recited (v) he asks Khadijah to cover him.

Working:
1. The worship in the cave comes first.
2. Then the command to read, the three embraces, the verses, and the return home.

Answer: (ii), (i), (iii), (iv), (v)

## Activity: Listen and narrate
You will need: A story of Cave Hira from a course book, a resource person, or an audio-visual clip
1. Watch or listen to the story of the Prophet's experience at Cave Hira.
2. In pairs, retell the story without looking at the book, and correct each other.
3. One learner narrates the story to the class in the right order.
4. Write five short sentences in your notebook that describe the incident.

## Practice
1. Where did Angel Jibril (A.S.) first come to the Prophet (S.A.W)?
2. What did the Prophet (S.A.W) reply when the angel first said 'Read'?
3. How many times did the angel embrace him before reciting the verses?
4. What did the Prophet (S.A.W) say to Khadijah (R.A.) when he reached home?

## Summary
• The Prophet (S.A.W) worshipped alone in Cave Hira before he was called.
• Jibril (A.S.) commanded him to read and embraced him three times.
• The first revelation was the opening of Surah Al-Alaq, and he returned trembling to Khadijah.

### Answers to practice
1. In the Cave of Hira.
2. He said he was not a reader.
3. Three times.
4. Cover me, cover me.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Khadijah's comfort and the news that he was a messenger

LESSON 2: KHADIJAH'S COMFORT AND THE NEWS THAT HE WAS A MESSENGER
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Describe how Khadijah (R.A.) responded after Cave Hira.
• State what Waraqah ibn Nawfal said about the revelation.
• Name one part of the Prophet's character to copy.

Curriculum outcomes: a) describe the Prophet’s incidence at cave Hira with Angel Jibril (A.S.); c) acknowledge the role of Prophet (S.A.W) as a messenger of Allah by emulating his Sunnah

## Introduction
A frightening honour had just been given to the Prophet (S.A.W). The first person to steady him was his wife. Her words tell us what kind of man Allah chose.

## Notes
### Khadijah (R.A.) comforts him
When the Prophet (S.A.W) told Khadijah (R.A.) what had happened, she did not mock him. She said, in meaning, that Allah would never disgrace him. She reminded him of his character: he kept good relations with his relatives, he spoke the truth, he helped the poor, he honoured the guest, and he supported those who were weak or in distress. This speech is in Sahih al-Bukhari.

Her comfort shows two things. First, good character was already his habit before prophethood. Second, a believing wife stands by her husband in fear as well as in joy. She then took him to her cousin, Waraqah ibn Nawfal.

### Waraqah ibn Nawfal
Waraqah was an old man who had become a Christian and who read the earlier scripture. When he heard the story, he said that this was the same angel, the Namus, whom Allah had sent to Musa (A.S.). He told the Prophet (S.A.W) that his people would drive him out. The Prophet (S.A.W) asked, "Will they drive me out?" Waraqah said that any man who came with a message like this was opposed. Waraqah died soon afterwards.

### A messenger to be followed
The incident at Hira was not a private dream to keep secret. It was the start of a message for people. The Prophet (S.A.W) later conveyed every verse, taught by his words and his actions, and did not hide the truth even when it was hard. Muslims acknowledge him as the Messenger of Allah by saying the shahadah and by copying his Sunnah: truthfulness, care for relatives, help for the weak, and honour for the guest. Those are the very qualities Khadijah named.

## Key words
• Khadijah (R.A.) — the wife of the Prophet (S.A.W) and the first person to believe in his message
• Waraqah ibn Nawfal — Khadijah's cousin, a Christian scholar who recognised the Prophet's revelation
• Sunnah — the teachings and practice of the Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W)
• shahadah — the declaration that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Khadijah listed five qualities of the Prophet (S.A.W). A learner wants to emulate him at school. Choose two of those qualities and say how they look in class.

Working:
1. The qualities include truthfulness, helping the weak, honouring a guest, joining family ties, and supporting people in distress.
2. School examples must be practical and honest.

Answer: Any two matching actions, for example telling the truth even when it is hard, and helping a classmate who has fallen or who has no pen.

## Activity: Read and retell
You will need: Reference material or the course book on the call to prophethood
1. Read the part of the story that follows the cave: Khadijah's comfort and the visit to Waraqah.
2. Close the book and narrate that part to a partner.
3. List the good qualities Khadijah mentioned and write them in your notebook.
4. Tick one quality you will practise this week as a way of following the Sunnah.

## Practice
1. Name two qualities Khadijah (R.A.) mentioned when she comforted the Prophet (S.A.W).
2. Who was Waraqah ibn Nawfal?
3. What did Waraqah say the people of Makkah would do?
4. How can a learner acknowledge the Prophet (S.A.W) as a messenger?

## Summary
• Khadijah (R.A.) comforted the Prophet and reminded him of his good character.
• Waraqah recognised the revelation and warned that the people would oppose him.
• Muslims follow the same character as part of his Sunnah.

### Answers to practice
1. Any two: he kept family ties, spoke the truth, helped the poor, honoured the guest, supported the weak.
2. Khadijah's elderly cousin, a Christian who recognised that the angel who came to the Prophet was the one sent to Musa (A.S.).
3. He said they would drive the Prophet (S.A.W) out.
4. By believing the shahadah and by copying his Sunnah, such as truthfulness and helping the weak.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq

LESSON 3: THE FIRST FIVE VERSES OF SURAH AL-ALAQ
================================================

## What you will learn
• Recite the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq.
• Give the meaning of each verse in simple English.

Curriculum outcomes: b) assess the significance of the first five verses revealed to Prophet (S.A.W) in relation to seeking knowledge

## Introduction
The first words sent down were not a long law. They were a command to read, and a reminder of Who created people and Who teaches them.

## Notes
### The five verses
Surah Al-Alaq is the 96th surah of the Qur'an. Its first five verses were the first revelation. Recite them slowly:

1. Iqra' bismi rabbikal-ladhi khalaq.
Read, in the name of your Lord who created.

2. Khalaqal-insana min 'alaq.
He created man from a clinging clot.

3. Iqra' wa rabbukal-akram.
Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.

4. Alladhi 'allama bil-qalam.
Who taught by the pen.

5. 'Allamal-insana ma lam ya'lam.
Taught man what he did not know.

### Meaning, line by line
- "Read" is also understood as "recite". The Prophet (S.A.W) was asked to recite by the power of Allah, not from a book he had studied. He had not been a reader.
- Reading is done in the name of the Lord. Knowledge is begun with Allah's name, just as a Muslim says Bismillah before other good acts.
- Allah created the human being from a clinging clot, a small beginning. The One who created people from that stage can also teach them.
- "Most Generous" means Allah gives freely. Guidance and knowledge are gifts, not things we boast about.
- The pen stands for writing. Allah taught people through what is written, so books, notes and the Qur'an itself matter.
- The last verse says people are taught what they did not know. No one is born already knowing the Qur'an, arithmetic or good manners. Learning is expected.

Practise until you can recite the five verses without looking. Reciting them is part of this sub-strand, and it should be done respectfully, in a clean state when you are reciting the Qur'an as worship.

## Key words
• Surah Al-Alaq — the 96th chapter of the Qur'an; its first five verses were the first revelation
• Iqra' — Read, or recite
• 'alaq — a clinging clot, the stage of creation named in the second verse
• qalam — the pen

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Match each phrase to its meaning: (i) Iqra' (ii) bil-qalam (iii) ma lam ya'lam.

Working:
1. Iqra' is the command to read or recite.
2. Al-qalam is the pen.
3. Ma lam ya'lam means what he did not know.

Answer: (i) Read or recite. (ii) By the pen. (iii) What he did not know.

## Activity: Recite Surah Al-Alaq 1-5
You will need: A chart or mushaf open at Surah Al-Alaq, Exercise book
1. Listen to a correct recitation of the first five verses.
2. Recite together, then individually or in groups, repeating until the words are clear.
3. Write the simple English meaning of each verse in your notebook.
4. A partner listens and kindly points out a word that needs practice.

## Practice
1. Which surah contains the first verses revealed to the Prophet (S.A.W)?
2. What is the meaning of the first verse?
3. What does the fourth verse say Allah taught by?
4. What is the meaning of the fifth verse?

## Summary
• The first command of the Qur'an is to read in the name of the Lord.
• Allah created people, and He is the Most Generous Teacher.
• He taught by the pen and taught people what they did not know.

### Answers to practice
1. Surah Al-Alaq.
2. Read, in the name of your Lord who created.
3. The pen.
4. He taught man what he did not know.

PAGE 5: Lesson 4: Seeking knowledge and following the Prophet's Sunnah

LESSON 4: SEEKING KNOWLEDGE AND FOLLOWING THE PROPHET'S SUNNAH
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Explain why the first five verses make seeking knowledge important.
• Give ways of emulating the Prophet (S.A.W) as Allah's Messenger.

Curriculum outcomes: b) assess the significance of the first five verses revealed to Prophet (S.A.W) in relation to seeking knowledge; c) acknowledge the role of Prophet (S.A.W) as a messenger of Allah by emulating his Sunnah

## Introduction
If the first word revealed was 'Read', then a Muslim learner is already inside the message when a book is opened for a good purpose. The cave and the classroom are connected.

## Notes
### Why these verses matter for knowledge
- The message of Islam began with reading, not with a call to be lazy or proud. Seeking knowledge is part of following the revelation.
- Knowledge is tied to Allah. We learn in His name, we thank Him for understanding, and we do not use knowledge to harm people or to show off.
- The pen shows that writing and careful study are gifts. Copying notes, reading the Qur'an and revising school work are ways of respecting that gift.
- People start without knowledge and are taught. Asking a teacher, repeating a verse, and admitting "I do not know yet" fit the fifth verse.
- The Most Generous Lord rewards the effort to learn. A learner who tries, even when a subject is hard, is answering Iqra'.

### Emulating the Messenger
Acknowledging the Prophet (S.A.W) is more than saying his name. His Sunnah after the call includes:

- Conveying the truth calmly and not hiding it.
- Being truthful, as he was before and after Hira.
- Caring for relatives and for people in need, the qualities Khadijah described.
- Worshipping Allah, including the prayer he later taught.
- Seeking knowledge of the Qur'an and acting on it.
- Being patient when people refuse the message, as he had to be in Makkah.

A Grade 4 learner emulates him in ways that fit a child's life: reciting the new verses correctly, telling the truth, helping a classmate, speaking well of parents, and beginning study with Bismillah. That is how love for the Messenger becomes action.

## Key words
• seek knowledge — to make an effort to learn what Allah has taught through revelation and through useful study
• emulate — to copy a good example
• revelation — what Allah sent down to the Prophet (S.A.W)

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Two learners revise Surah Al-Alaq. One laughs at the other for reading slowly. Which learner is closer to the teaching of the first five verses?

Working:
1. The verses say Allah taught people what they did not know. Learning takes effort.
2. Mocking a learner goes against the character of the Prophet (S.A.W).

Answer: The learner who reads patiently and helps a classmate is closer to the verses and to the Sunnah.

## Activity: What the five verses ask of us
You will need: Exercise book, The chart of Surah Al-Alaq 1-5
1. In pairs, discuss the significance of the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq for seeking knowledge.
2. Write four points in your notebook.
3. Add two ways you will emulate the Prophet (S.A.W) this week.
4. Present one point to the class and listen to other views with respect.

## Practice
1. Why is the command 'Read' important for a Muslim learner?
2. How does the mention of the pen encourage study?
3. Give two ways a learner can emulate the Prophet (S.A.W).

## Summary
• The first revelation makes seeking knowledge part of Islam.
• Learning is done in Allah's name and without mocking others.
• Muslims acknowledge the Messenger by copying his Sunnah in daily life.

### Answers to practice
1. Because the first revelation begins with reading, so seeking knowledge is part of the message.
2. It shows that Allah taught by writing, so books, notes and careful reading are a gift to be used.
3. Any two: tell the truth, help people in need, keep good family ties, recite the Qur'an, begin work with Bismillah, be patient.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 7.1 CALL TO PROPHETHOOD
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Where was the Prophet (S.A.W) when the first revelation came?
   A. the market of Taif
   B. Cave Hira
   C. the mosque of Madinah
   D. a ship

2. What did Jibril (A.S.) first say?
   A. Sleep
   B. Read
   C. Build
   D. Trade

3. How did the Prophet (S.A.W) answer before the verses were recited?

4. When he reached home, what did he say to Khadijah?
   A. Cover me, cover me
   B. Send the people away forever
   C. I will not tell you
   D. Close the school

5. Khadijah (R.A.) said Allah would not disgrace him because of which of these?
   A. wealth only
   B. good character, such as truthfulness and helping the weak
   C. fame in poetry
   D. large army

6. Waraqah ibn Nawfal said this angel was the one who used to come to whom?
   A. Fir'awn
   B. Musa (A.S.)
   C. the traders only
   D. the children of Taif

7. The first five verses are from Surah…
   A. Al-Fatihah
   B. Al-Alaq
   C. Al-Nas
   D. Al-Ikhlas

8. The fourth verse teaches that Allah taught by which of these?
   A. sword
   B. pen
   C. drum
   D. market

9. Why do these verses make seeking knowledge important?

10. How does a learner emulate the Prophet (S.A.W)?
   A. hiding the truth
   B. telling the truth and helping the weak
   C. mocking a slow reader
   D. refusing to recite

11. What does 'He taught man what he did not know' encourage?
   A. Pride
   B. Effort in learning
   C. Leaving school
   D. Laughing at teachers
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 7.1 CALL TO PROPHETHOOD
========================================

1. B. Cave Hira
   He was worshipping in Cave Hira when Jibril (A.S.) came.

2. B. Read
   The command was Iqra', Read.

3. He said that he was not a reader.
   He had not been taught to read. The recitation came by revelation.

4. A. Cover me, cover me
   He was trembling and asked to be wrapped until he became calm.

5. B. good character, such as truthfulness and helping the weak
   She named his truth, family ties, help for the poor, honour for guests and support for the weak.

6. B. Musa (A.S.)
   He recognised the revelation as the same kind sent to Musa (A.S.).

7. B. Al-Alaq
   Surah Al-Alaq, chapter 96, begins with Iqra'.

8. B. pen
   Alladhi 'allama bil-qalam means He who taught by the pen.

9. The revelation begins with 'Read', mentions the pen, and says Allah taught people what they did not know.
   Learning is at the start of the message of Islam.

10. B. telling the truth and helping the weak
   Those qualities are part of his Sunnah and were praised by Khadijah.

11. B. Effort in learning
   People are not born with this knowledge, so they are taught.

===========================================

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Put these events in order: (i) Jibril says Read (ii) the Prophet worships in Cave Hira (iii) the angel embraces him three times (iv) the first verses are recited (v) he asks Khadijah to cover him.

Working:
1. The worship in the cave comes first.
2. Then the command to read, the three embraces, the verses, and the return home.

## Practice
1. Where did Angel Jibril (A.S.) first come to the Prophet (S.A.W)?
2. What did the Prophet (S.A.W) reply when the angel first said 'Read'?
3. How many times did the angel embrace him before reciting the verses?
4. What did the Prophet (S.A.W) say to Khadijah (R.A.) when he reached home?

## Summary
• The Prophet (S.A.W) worshipped alone in Cave Hira before he was called.
• Jibril (A.S.) commanded him to read and embraced him three times.
• The first revelation was the opening of Surah Al-Alaq, and he returned trembling to Khadijah.

### Answers to practice
1. In the Cave of Hira.
2. He said he was not a reader.
3. Three times.
4. Cover me, cover me.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Khadijah's comfort and the news that he was a messenger
studyPages.body:
LESSON 2: KHADIJAH'S COMFORT AND THE NEWS THAT HE WAS A MESSENGER
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Describe how Khadijah (R.A.) responded after Cave Hira.
• State what Waraqah ibn Nawfal said about the revelation.
• Name one part of the Prophet's character to copy.

Curriculum outcomes: a) describe the Prophet’s incidence at cave Hira with Angel Jibril (A.S.); c) acknowledge the role of Prophet (S.A.W) as a messenger of Allah by emulating his Sunnah

## Introduction
A frightening honour had just been given to the Prophet (S.A.W). The first person to steady him was his wife. Her words tell us what kind of man Allah chose.

## Notes
### Khadijah (R.A.) comforts him
When the Prophet (S.A.W) told Khadijah (R.A.) what had happened, she did not mock him. She said, in meaning, that Allah would never disgrace him. She reminded him of his character: he kept good relations with his relatives, he spoke the truth, he helped the poor, he honoured the guest, and he supported those who were weak or in distress. This speech is in Sahih al-Bukhari.

Her comfort shows two things. First, good character was already his habit before prophethood. Second, a believing wife stands by her husband in fear as well as in joy. She then took him to her cousin, Waraqah ibn Nawfal.

### Waraqah ibn Nawfal
Waraqah was an old man who had become a Christian and who read the earlier scripture. When he heard the story, he said that this was the same angel, the Namus, whom Allah had sent to Musa (A.S.). He told the Prophet (S.A.W) that his people would drive him out. The Prophet (S.A.W) asked, "Will they drive me out?" Waraqah said that any man who came with a message like this was opposed. Waraqah died soon afterwards.

### A messenger to be followed
The incident at Hira was not a private dream to keep secret. It was the start of a message for people. The Prophet (S.A.W) later conveyed every verse, taught by his words and his actions, and did not hide the truth even when it was hard. Muslims acknowledge him as the Messenger of Allah by saying the shahadah and by copying his Sunnah: truthfulness, care for relatives, help for the weak, and honour for the guest. Those are the very qualities Khadijah named.

## Key words
• Khadijah (R.A.) — the wife of the Prophet (S.A.W) and the first person to believe in his message
• Waraqah ibn Nawfal — Khadijah's cousin, a Christian scholar who recognised the Prophet's revelation
• Sunnah — the teachings and practice of the Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W)
• shahadah — the declaration that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Khadijah listed five qualities of the Prophet (S.A.W). A learner wants to emulate him at school. Choose two of those qualities and say how they look in class.

Working:
1. The qualities include truthfulness, helping the weak, honouring a guest, joining family ties, and supporting people in distress.
2. School examples must be practical and honest.

Answer: Any two matching actions, for example telling the truth even when it is hard, and helping a classmate who has fallen or who has no pen.

## Activity: Read and retell
You will need: Reference material or the course book on the call to prophethood
1. Read the part of the story that follows the cave: Khadijah's comfort and the visit to Waraqah.
2. Close the book and narrate that part to a partner.
3. List the good qualities Khadijah mentioned and write them in your notebook.
4. Tick one quality you will practise this week as a way of following the Sunnah.

## Practice
1. Name two qualities Khadijah (R.A.) mentioned when she comforted the Prophet (S.A.W).
2. Who was Waraqah ibn Nawfal?
3. What did Waraqah say the people of Makkah would do?
4. How can a learner acknowledge the Prophet (S.A.W) as a messenger?

## Summary
• Khadijah (R.A.) comforted the Prophet and reminded him of his good character.
• Waraqah recognised the revelation and warned that the people would oppose him.
• Muslims follow the same character as part of his Sunnah.

### Answers to practice
1. Any two: he kept family ties, spoke the truth, helped the poor, honoured the guest, supported the weak.
2. Khadijah's elderly cousin, a Christian who recognised that the angel who came to the Prophet was the one sent to Musa (A.S.).
3. He said they would drive the Prophet (S.A.W) out.
4. By believing the shahadah and by copying his Sunnah, such as truthfulness and helping the weak.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq
studyPages.body:
LESSON 3: THE FIRST FIVE VERSES OF SURAH AL-ALAQ
================================================

## What you will learn
• Recite the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq.
• Give the meaning of each verse in simple English.

Curriculum outcomes: b) assess the significance of the first five verses revealed to Prophet (S.A.W) in relation to seeking knowledge

## Introduction
The first words sent down were not a long law. They were a command to read, and a reminder of Who created people and Who teaches them.

## Notes
### The five verses
Surah Al-Alaq is the 96th surah of the Qur'an. Its first five verses were the first revelation. Recite them slowly:

1. Iqra' bismi rabbikal-ladhi khalaq.
Read, in the name of your Lord who created.

2. Khalaqal-insana min 'alaq.
He created man from a clinging clot.

3. Iqra' wa rabbukal-akram.
Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.

4. Alladhi 'allama bil-qalam.
Who taught by the pen.

5. 'Allamal-insana ma lam ya'lam.
Taught man what he did not know.

### Meaning, line by line
- "Read" is also understood as "recite". The Prophet (S.A.W) was asked to recite by the power of Allah, not from a book he had studied. He had not been a reader.
- Reading is done in the name of the Lord. Knowledge is begun with Allah's name, just as a Muslim says Bismillah before other good acts.
- Allah created the human being from a clinging clot, a small beginning. The One who created people from that stage can also teach them.
- "Most Generous" means Allah gives freely. Guidance and knowledge are gifts, not things we boast about.
- The pen stands for writing. Allah taught people through what is written, so books, notes and the Qur'an itself matter.
- The last verse says people are taught what they did not know. No one is born already knowing the Qur'an, arithmetic or good manners. Learning is expected.

Practise until you can recite the five verses without looking. Reciting them is part of this sub-strand, and it should be done respectfully, in a clean state when you are reciting the Qur'an as worship.

## Key words
• Surah Al-Alaq — the 96th chapter of the Qur'an; its first five verses were the first revelation
• Iqra' — Read, or recite
• 'alaq — a clinging clot, the stage of creation named in the second verse
• qalam — the pen

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Match each phrase to its meaning: (i) Iqra' (ii) bil-qalam (iii) ma lam ya'lam.

Working:
1. Iqra' is the command to read or recite.
2. Al-qalam is the pen.
3. Ma lam ya'lam means what he did not know.

Answer: (i) Read or recite. (ii) By the pen. (iii) What he did not know.

## Activity: Recite Surah Al-Alaq 1-5
You will need: A chart or mushaf open at Surah Al-Alaq, Exercise book
1. Listen to a correct recitation of the first five verses.
2. Recite together, then individually or in groups, repeating until the words are clear.
3. Write the simple English meaning of each verse in your notebook.
4. A partner listens and kindly points out a word that needs practice.

## Practice
1. Which surah contains the first verses revealed to the Prophet (S.A.W)?
2. What is the meaning of the first verse?
3. What does the fourth verse say Allah taught by?
4. What is the meaning of the fifth verse?

## Summary
• The first command of the Qur'an is to read in the name of the Lord.
• Allah created people, and He is the Most Generous Teacher.
• He taught by the pen and taught people what they did not know.

### Answers to practice
1. Surah Al-Alaq.
2. Read, in the name of your Lord who created.
3. The pen.
4. He taught man what he did not know.

studyPages.title: Lesson 4: Seeking knowledge and following the Prophet's Sunnah
studyPages.body:
LESSON 4: SEEKING KNOWLEDGE AND FOLLOWING THE PROPHET'S SUNNAH
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Explain why the first five verses make seeking knowledge important.
• Give ways of emulating the Prophet (S.A.W) as Allah's Messenger.

Curriculum outcomes: b) assess the significance of the first five verses revealed to Prophet (S.A.W) in relation to seeking knowledge; c) acknowledge the role of Prophet (S.A.W) as a messenger of Allah by emulating his Sunnah

## Introduction
If the first word revealed was 'Read', then a Muslim learner is already inside the message when a book is opened for a good purpose. The cave and the classroom are connected.

## Notes
### Why these verses matter for knowledge
- The message of Islam began with reading, not with a call to be lazy or proud. Seeking knowledge is part of following the revelation.
- Knowledge is tied to Allah. We learn in His name, we thank Him for understanding, and we do not use knowledge to harm people or to show off.
- The pen shows that writing and careful study are gifts. Copying notes, reading the Qur'an and revising school work are ways of respecting that gift.
- People start without knowledge and are taught. Asking a teacher, repeating a verse, and admitting "I do not know yet" fit the fifth verse.
- The Most Generous Lord rewards the effort to learn. A learner who tries, even when a subject is hard, is answering Iqra'.

### Emulating the Messenger
Acknowledging the Prophet (S.A.W) is more than saying his name. His Sunnah after the call includes:

- Conveying the truth calmly and not hiding it.
- Being truthful, as he was before and after Hira.
- Caring for relatives and for people in need, the qualities Khadijah described.
- Worshipping Allah, including the prayer he later taught.
- Seeking knowledge of the Qur'an and acting on it.
- Being patient when people refuse the message, as he had to be in Makkah.

A Grade 4 learner emulates him in ways that fit a child's life: reciting the new verses correctly, telling the truth, helping a classmate, speaking well of parents, and beginning study with Bismillah. That is how love for the Messenger becomes action.

## Key words
• seek knowledge — to make an effort to learn what Allah has taught through revelation and through useful study
• emulate — to copy a good example
• revelation — what Allah sent down to the Prophet (S.A.W)

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Two learners revise Surah Al-Alaq. One laughs at the other for reading slowly. Which learner is closer to the teaching of the first five verses?

Working:
1. The verses say Allah taught people what they did not know. Learning takes effort.
2. Mocking a learner goes against the character of the Prophet (S.A.W).

Answer: The learner who reads patiently and helps a classmate is closer to the verses and to the Sunnah.

## Activity: What the five verses ask of us
You will need: Exercise book, The chart of Surah Al-Alaq 1-5
1. In pairs, discuss the significance of the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq for seeking knowledge.
2. Write four points in your notebook.
3. Add two ways you will emulate the Prophet (S.A.W) this week.
4. Present one point to the class and listen to other views with respect.

## Practice
1. Why is the command 'Read' important for a Muslim learner?
2. How does the mention of the pen encourage study?
3. Give two ways a learner can emulate the Prophet (S.A.W).

## Summary
• The first revelation makes seeking knowledge part of Islam.
• Learning is done in Allah's name and without mocking others.
• Muslims acknowledge the Messenger by copying his Sunnah in daily life.

### Answers to practice
1. Because the first revelation begins with reading, so seeking knowledge is part of the message.
2. It shows that Allah taught by writing, so books, notes and careful reading are a gift to be used.
3. Any two: tell the truth, help people in need, keep good family ties, recite the Qur'an, begin work with Bismillah, be patient.
